question: What is the primary characteristic of cancer cells?
explanation: Cancer occurs when cellular regulation fails, leading to unchecked division and invasion of surrounding tissues. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why is the primary health care nurse vital in cancer management?

options.A: They provide the first contact and early referral
options.C: They perform complex surgical resections locally
options.D: They manage final end-stage hospice admissions

explanation: Primary care nurses spot early warning signs and direct patients to specialized centers for prompt diagnosis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h1)

question: The spread of cancer cells to distant body organs is called:
explanation: Metastasis describes the migration of malignant cells via blood or lymph to form secondary tumors elsewhere. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h2)

question: What happens during the initiation phase of carcinogenesis?

options.A: Tumors develop a dedicated blood supply system
options.B: Permanent damage occurs to the cellular DNA
options.C: Malignant cells travel through the lymphatic system
options.D: Immune cells completely destroy the mutated tissue

explanation: Initiation is the foundational step where an irreversible mutation alters the genetic code of a normal cell. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h2)

question: Which cancer has the highest incidence among Nigerian women?
explanation: Breast cancer remains the most prevalent malignancy affecting women in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h3)

question: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of human papillomavirus directly causes:
explanation: Human papillomavirus is the primary viral agent responsible for the development of cervical malignancies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h3)

question: Which viral infection is strongly linked to hepatocellular carcinoma in Nigeria?
explanation: Chronic Hepatitis B and C infections are major risk factors for liver cancer development. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h4)

question: Why is family history considered a significant cancer risk factor?

options.A: It guarantees the person will develop malignant tumors
options.B: It measures the effectiveness of childhood vaccinations
options.C: It proves environmental contamination within the household
options.D: It indicates inherited gene mutations that raise susceptibility

explanation: Inherited mutations in specific genes pass through families, increasing the baseline lifetime risk for certain cancers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h4)

question: What is the main goal of cancer screening programs in primary care?

options.A: Detecting pre-cancerous changes or early asymptomatic disease
options.B: Confirming the exact histological grade of a biopsy
options.C: Providing definitive surgical removal of advanced tumors
options.D: Administering palliative chemotherapy for end-stage pain

explanation: Screening aims to identify abnormalities before symptoms arise, when treatment is most successful. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a routine primary care screening method?
explanation: PET scans are advanced diagnostic imaging tools used in specialized tertiary centers, not routine primary care screening tests. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is required to confirm a definitive diagnosis of cancer?
explanation: Microscopic examination of tissue cells by a pathologist provides the only definitive diagnosis of malignancy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h6)

question: A patient presenting with unexplained rapid weight loss and persistent fatigue warrants:

options.B: Routine follow-up in six months if pain occurs
options.C: Diagnosis of a simple vitamin deficiency state
options.D: Prompt clinical investigation for underlying malignancy

explanation: Constitutional symptoms like unexplained weight loss are hallmark red flags requiring thorough diagnostic evaluation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h6)

question: What tool guides the pharmacological management of cancer pain?
explanation: The World Health Organization analgesic ladder provides a step-by-step approach to managing cancer pain effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h7)

question: Why is monitoring white blood cell counts critical during chemotherapy?

options.A: To prevent sudden severe hair loss
options.B: To measure direct tumor shrinkage rates
options.C: To detect immunosuppression and infection risk
options.D: To evaluate the nutritional protein status

explanation: Chemotherapy suppresses bone marrow function, lowering white blood cells and predisposing patients to severe infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care in advanced cancer?

options.A: Improving quality of life and relieving distressing symptoms
options.B: Hastening the natural death process to reduce costs
options.C: Executing aggressive surgical cures for terminal metastasis
options.D: Testing experimental curative medications on patients

explanation: Palliative care centers on comfort, pain management, and holistic support when curative treatment is no longer possible. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h8)

question: Community cancer education by nurses primarily aims to:

options.B: Promote early presentation and dispel myths
options.D: Train community members to perform biopsies

explanation: Educational outreach targets fear and misconceptions, encouraging people to seek medical evaluation early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h8)
